premises: Fast segregation of Cr, Mn, Ni to grain boundaries in CrMnFeCoNi HEA causes ductility loss at intermediate temperatures
Preexisting precipitates can capture segregating embrittling elements and evade ductility loss
Ductility loss in coarse-grained CrMnFeCoNi HEA at ~650°C is not due to intermetallic formation, oxidation, or hydrogen embrittlement
Grain-boundary nanoclusters of principal elements reduce interfacial cohesion and trigger intergranular fracture
The effect is specific to intermediate temperatures (~600–700°C) where segregation kinetics compete with deformation
